notice: Light Saturday edition — research and opensource scouts returned empty, so today's Lens is leaner than usual. The stories that made it earned their place.

lead.title: Claude Opus 5 lands at half the price of Fable 5 — and Anthropic says it's better
lead.summary: Anthropic's new flagship doesn't just match the competition — it undercuts it. Opus 5 is pitched as a step-change for long-running agents and professional coding work, arriving at roughly half the cost of Fable 5 while claiming wins on Anthropic's own benchmarks. The pricing move matters more than the model itself: frontier capability is becoming a commodity, and Anthropic just made that explicit.

top_stories.title: South Korea pledges trillions for AI semiconductors, with Huang, Altman, and Amodei on stage
top_stories.summary: President Lee Jae Myung's 'San Francisco AI Declaration' isn't just rhetoric — it's a multitrillion-dollar commitment to AI chips, hyperscale data centers, and physical AI. The NVIDIA-KAIST joint lab, a first between a Korean university and a global tech giant, signals Seoul intends to own a piece of the AI stack, not just buy it.

top_stories.title: The real question behind AMD's Helios: can it chase NVIDIA's margin, not just its performance?
top_stories.summary: The Next Platform's deep-dive into AMD's rack-scale roadmap cuts through the launch hype. Helios claims 30% more inference tokens per dollar than Vera Rubin NVL72, but the analysis asks the harder question: whether AMD's integrated approach can sustain the financial momentum through Helios 500 and 600 out to 2030.

items.title: Intel plans fresh layoffs in Data Center Group amid Lip-Bu Tan's restructuring
items.summary: The cuts target Intel's server CPU, AI chip, and data center architecture division — the very unit meant to compete with NVIDIA and AMD. Tan calls it focus; it reads more like retreat from a market Intel once defined.

items.title: AI4I's SUK platform gets full-page treatment in Il Sole 24 Ore
items.summary: The Italian Institute for AI's technology transfer platform connects 140 AI providers, 59 startups, and 70 SMEs through structured matching. The mainstream business press coverage suggests Italy's industrial AI adoption is moving from pilot to pipeline.

items.title: Italy's national AI committee chair: stop the hype, start the science
items.summary: Gianluigi Greco argues public AI debate is trapped between alarmism and unrealistic expectation. His call for 'strategic decisions anchored in scientific rigor' is a direct challenge to both doomers and boosters in Italy's policy circles.

items.title: Emilia-Romagna's Food Valley uses AI to push Italian agrifood into global markets
items.summary: The region isn't just using AI to optimize production — it's leveraging it for international expansion. A reminder that some of the most consequential AI deployments happen far from datacenters and model benchmarks.
